title: Uniform left-half-plane resolvents and harmonic-oscillator norm approximation for monotone quadratic imaginary Dirichlet potentials
source_title: Critical time for the observability of Kolmogorov-type equations
author: Jérémi Dardé; Julien Royer
difficulty_reason: Separate harmonic and Airy resolvent bounds do not control the variable-coefficient Dirichlet operator uniformly over the expanding spectral half-plane. The author builds two compatible localization scales, controls Taylor and commutator errors, and sums a growing family of local inverse operators using almost orthogonality. A further zero-resolvent comparison removes the cutoff and gives the required little-o model error.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Independent Proposition3.6 for finite interval I=(−ell_minus,ell_plus), real q in C3 of the closed interval, q(0)=0 and min qprime>0, Kn=−d²/dy²+i n q² with Dirichlet domain, gamma in(0,qprime(0)/sqrt2). Both uniform O(n^−1/2) resolvent bound and zero-extended inverse norm approximation to the complex harmonic oscillator are selected. Full two-scale cutoff choice, Airy boundary localization, commutator estimates and almost-orthogonal summation retained. Classical complex harmonic oscillator and whole/half-line Airy resolvent results are explicit named existing research prerequisites. No critical-time or two-sided Agmon boundary estimate selected:3.24 signed integral of a nonnegative square-root integrand is negative for y<0, while3.11 compares it to a positive integral of q; that separate displayed left-side weight mismatch is outside the selected resolvent core.
